content.title: About
content.content: Summer squash (zucchini) is the young, tender fruit of the plant Cucurbita pepo. Green raw zucchini has a mild, slightly sweet flavor and a crisp texture. It is commonly used in fresh salads, as a snack, or in dishes that require quick cooking.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Zucchini belongs to the gourd family and is one of the fastest‑growing vegetables – first fruits appear 45–55 days after sowing.
Green summer squash is often called “summer pumpkin,” though botanically it is not a pumpkin.
Raw zucchini is over 90 % water, making it very low‑calorie.
It has many names worldwide: Italian “zucchina,” French “courgette,” etc.
The edible part is the immature fruit; if it overripens the skin becomes bitter and tough.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: One cup (≈124 g) of raw zucchini provides about 30 % of the daily vitamin C requirement, supporting immunity and antioxidant defense.

items.title: Good source of potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and blood pressure; 100 g of zucchini contains roughly 300 mg.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: Raw zucchini contains about 17 kcal per 100 g, making it an excellent choice for weight‑controlled diets.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Lutein and zeaxanthin in zucchini support eye health.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience an allergic reaction to cucurbit vegetables, including zucchini.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: When buying non‑organic produce, rinse zucchini thoroughly to remove possible chemical residues.

items.title: Food safety
items.content: Over‑ripe fruits can develop bitter cucurbitacins; such zucchini should not be eaten raw.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Raw zucchini can be sliced into thin strips or rounds and added to salads, used in wraps, or made into “zoodles” (zucchini noodles). It can also be lightly sautéed, baked, or steamed to retain its crunch and nutrients.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store zucchini in the refrigerator’s vegetable drawer, wrapped in a perforated bag. It stays fresh for 5–7 days. Discard any pieces that become soft, slimy, or develop an off‑odor.
